demo_mode.notes: This meets two of the three playbook criteria fully (deterministic-ish seeds, explicit blocking of durable writes) and sidesteps auth entirely by having no Firebase, but it has NO mode gate — the criterion the playbook lists first. It is a hard fork frozen in demo state rather than a mode of a product, so it cannot be flipped back to real behaviour and cannot receive upstream fixes. Seeds are only semi-deterministic: IDs are stable slugs but createdAt/updatedAt are computed from Date.now() at boot (src/app/useAppState.js:100,116-117). Mutations DO persist: the shelf is written to localStorage (hearth_template_items_v1), so a visitor's marks/vibes survive reload and there is no reset-to-seed affordance — unlike hearth_v2 template mode, which is in-memory and resets on refresh.

deploy.kind: GitHub Pages from committed docs/ build output (no Actions workflow — manual build+commit)
deploy.evidence: package.json homepage='https://benwassa.github.io/template-hearth'; build script sets BUILD_PATH=docs; docs/index.html and docs/static are committed; .nojekyll re-added in three recent commits; no .github/ directory exists

stack: express + cors + dotenv listed as deps but unused in the template build
readiness.build_cmd: npm run build (DISABLE_ESLINT_PLUGIN=true BUILD_PATH=docs react-scripts build)
screenshots: public/posters/*.jpg (45 real poster images — good visual material for a card)
readiness.one_liner: A calm shared watchlist for couples: a pre-seeded shelf of 45 films and shows with posters, a nightly 'Tonight' tray, vibe/energy tagging, and a decision helper that picks something to watch for you.

drift_flags: package.json name is 'hearth' and version 3.7.1 — inherited from the upstream product, so the fork advertises a version number it does not actually track. Upstream hearth_v2 has moved to HEAD 2026-08-15, roughly 6.5 months ahead of this fork's 2026-01-30.

README calls add/import/export 'dummy features' but the UI still renders full working Add and Import forms (src/views/AddView.js, src/views/ImportModal.js) that only fail at submit time with a toast — a visitor can fill in a whole form before being told it does nothing.
Dependencies express, cors, dotenv and the DISABLE_ESLINT_PLUGIN build flag are leftovers from the server-backed original; there is no server in this repo.
Deploy is manual (committed docs/ output, no CI). Three of the five most recent commits are 'Re-add .nojekyll' — the Pages setup was fought with rather than automated.
Built on react-scripts (CRA), which upstream hearth_v2 has left behind for Vite (hearth_v2 uses import.meta.env / VITE_HEARTH_MODE) — the two codebases can no longer share code without a port.
Mutations persist to localStorage with no reset control, so a visitor can permanently scramble the demo shelf in their own browser.
rationale: The demo experience it provides is real and embeddable, but it is now strictly dominated: hearth_v2 (HEAD 2026-08-15) implements the same experience as a proper mode of the live product, with a mode gate, ephemeral state, and auth isolation. Keeping this fork means maintaining a 6.5-month-stale CRA copy of a Vite product to get something the product already does.

template_fork_comparison.question: Does hearth_v2 have demo affordances template-hearth was created to provide?
template_fork_comparison.answer: YES — comprehensively, and better. hearth_v2/src/app/useConfiguredAppState.js is a real mode resolver: VITE_HEARTH_MODE=template, ?mode=demo, ?mode=template, or ?demo=1 all swap useAppState for useTemplateAppState. It ships hearth_v2/src/template/seedLibrary.js (30 curated titles with stable IDs AND stable timestamps), seed-media-map.json for pre-generated metadata, and a documented playbook at hearth_v2/docs/DEMO_STATE_PLAYBOOK.md.
template_fork_comparison.what_the_fork_still_does_uniquely: Almost nothing of value. Two marginal differences: (1) it carries 45 seeded titles vs hearth_v2's 30, and (2) its mutations persist to localStorage where hearth_v2's demo state is in-memory and resets on refresh — that is arguably a defect, not a feature, since a portfolio embed wants a clean slate for each visitor. Everything else it offers (no-Firebase operation, disabled import/export, seeded shelf) hearth_v2 does natively, plus auth sandboxing (anonymous auth, sign-out of real sessions, hearth* storage keys cleared) that this fork has no equivalent for because it has no auth at all.
template_fork_comparison.verdict: REDUNDANT. Replace the portfolio embed with hearth_v2 at ?mode=demo and retire template-hearth (archive, do not delete — it is the historical origin of the demo pattern). The one thing to verify before switching is that hearth_v2's deployed build actually honours ?mode=demo in production.
